title: Local depth estimates reduce the mean dip-change correlation from 0.20 to -0.03 in 39 selected TESS complex periodic variables
abstract: We test whether dips at separate phases change together in complex periodic variables (CPVs). A shared supply or common clearing of occulting material could cause such changes. We reuse released per-cycle dip depths and retrieve 77 exact TESS SPOC light curves. Shared subtraction of harmonics 0-2 mixes real dip signals and their white noise; we derive its response matrix and a diagnostic correction. We also measure local depths from each dip and four shoulder bins, with disjoint phase samples between selected pairs. On identical temporal contrast boundaries for 190 region pairs in 76 sectors of 39 stars, the published depths give a star-mean correlation of 0.202 (95% star-resampling interval 0.123 to 0.286). Local quadratic depths give -0.027 (-0.089 to 0.029); the paired difference is 0.229 (0.133 to 0.333). The model-based adjusted score is 0.009 (-0.055 to 0.075). Shared Gaussian depth changes with width 0.025 cycles and RMS 0.3% of stellar flux are recovered above the observed upper interval endpoint in 199 of 200 draws. This is a conditional sensitivity check, not a physical exclusion limit. An exploratory excess of unsigned local correlation remains, but depends on timescale and an unvalidated circular-shift reference. Thus the positive mean of the published depths is not secure evidence for common feeding or clearing. The local null does not establish independent clumps: broad changes are suppressed, opposite signs can cancel, and fixed phase regions need not trace material. We provide code, attributed input tables, phase-bin means, exact raw paths, URLs, hashes and all aggregate and pair results.

display.caption: On identical boundaries in 39 stars, the mean correlation changes from 0.202 for published depths to -0.027 for local depths. Intervals resample stars.
The exact equal-bin response shows that shared harmonic subtraction mixes independent dip amplitudes and their measurement noise. Local contrast supports are disjoint for selected pairs.
Shared-change sensitivity depends on dip width. The unsigned dependence is exploratory and depends on the temporal reference.
